title: Sagarmala Finance Corporation Starts Lending With Rs 4,300 Crore Approvals, Eyes Rs 8,000 Crore Loan Book And Greenfield Port Funding
text:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Jan 01, 2026 | Updated 10:43 AM GMT+5:30

Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL), the country’s first Non-Banking Financial Company dedicated entirely to maritime infrastructure, has formally commenced lending.
The corporation, which was inaugurated in June 2025, confirmed that its Board has sanctioned loans worth nearly Rs 4,300 crore during its 51st meeting held on 30 December 2025.
These approvals form part of an aggressive scale-up strategy endorsed at its Annual General Meeting, where the Board cleared a borrowing ceiling of Rs 25,000 crore and set a lending goal of Rs 8,000 crore for FY 2025-26.
The sanctioned projects, due for disbursal before the end of the fiscal, are expected to position SMFCL firmly within the domestic maritime finance ecosystem, creating an Rs 8,000 crore loan book in its very first operational year.
A substantial portion of the sanctions, approximately Rs 4,000 crore, will support the development of a Greenfield Port Project.
Alongside this, Dredging Corporation of India has secured Rs 150 crore, and Goa Shipyard is set to receive Rs 110 crore, strengthening both dredging capabilities and indigenous shipbuilding infrastructure.
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal described the moment as a key milestone.
SMFCL is also awaiting credit ratings from major rating agencies, which are expected to lower borrowing costs as it scales.
The corporation additionally serves as nodal agency for operationalising the Maritime Development Fund, which carries a Rs 25,000 crore corpus, and will manage government contributions to the Maritime Investment Fund in a fiduciary role.
